name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
disclaimer: Illustrative geometry at a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm). The GB202 die size (~750 mm²) and GDDR7 chip count/footprint are third-party reported, not officially published by NVIDIA in exact mm² or chip-count form. SM grid, RT core, texture unit, ROP and video-engine block counts are symbolic, not drawn to exact silicon layout. Covers the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation/Server/Max-Q Editions, which share the same GB202 ASIC and spec sheet — only cooling and form factor differ.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Standard organic flip-chip substrate, like a gaming GPU board. No silicon interposer or CoWoS bridge is needed — GDDR7 chips wire-bond straight to the substrate, unlike HBM-equipped data-center parts (B200, Rubin).

components.name: GB202 compute die
components.desc: A single monolithic die — GB202, NVIDIA's flagship RTX Blackwell GPU, also used (cut-down) in the GeForce RTX 5090. The RTX PRO 6000 enables 188 of the full die's 192 SMs. Holds SMs, a unified 128 MB L2, GDDR7 memory controllers, RT Cores, texture units, ROPs and video engines — everything on one piece of silicon, no die-to-die link like B200's two-die MCM.

specs.label: Full die config
specs.value: 12 GPCs, 96 TPCs, 192 SMs, 512-bit memory interface (16 x 32-bit controllers)

specs.label: SMs enabled (this card)
specs.value: 188 of 192 (full GB202 die, 4 disabled for yield)

specs.label: Die size
specs.value: ~750 mm² (third-party reported; NVIDIA has not published an exact mm² figure)

specs.label: Process
specs.value: TSMC 4N-class (widely reported as N4P; not officially specified by NVIDIA)

components.name: L2 cache
components.desc: 128 MB of unified L2 cache shared by all 188 SMs — one die, one cache, no NV-HBI coherency link to manage like B200's two dies. Buffers KV cache and weight tiles between GDDR7 and the SMs.

components.name: GDDR7 memory controllers (left)
components.desc: Half of the 512-bit GDDR7 PHY (16 x 32-bit controllers total). GDDR7 with on-die ECC gives data integrity without the capacity tax of HBM's dedicated ECC bits — fewer, faster pins per byte than HBM, lower cost and package area for a given capacity.

components.name: GDDR7 memory controllers (right)
components.desc: Other half of the 512-bit GDDR7 PHY.

components.name: RT Cores (4th gen)
components.desc: 188 fourth-generation RT Cores (one per SM), new with Mega Geometry (cluster-based BVH for huge scenes), Linear Swept Spheres for curves/hair, an Opacity Micromap engine and a Triangle Cluster Compression engine. Pure graphics/visualization hardware — absent on AI-only parts like B200.

components.name: Texture units
components.desc: 752 texture units (4 per SM) feed filtered texture data to shaders for rasterized and ray-traced rendering.

components.name: ROPs
components.desc: 192 raster operations units (8 per GPC partition x 2 partitions x 12 GPCs) write finished pixels to the frame buffer — workstation/visualization hardware with no equivalent on compute-only data-center GPUs.

components.name: Video encode/decode engines
components.desc: 4x ninth-generation NVENC encoders + 4x sixth-generation NVDEC decoders — useful for multimodal pre/post-processing pipelines as well as professional video workflows.

components.name: PCIe 5.0 x16
components.desc: Host and (where used) peer-to-peer connectivity is PCIe 5.0 x16 only — this card has no NVLink. That caps multi-GPU bandwidth well below NVLink-equipped data-center parts (e.g. B200's 1.8 TB/s NVLink 5 per GPU) but keeps the board a standard add-in card for workstations and PCIe-based servers.

specs.label: NVLink
specs.value: None — PCIe only (unlike NVLink-equipped data-center Blackwell GPUs)

components.name: SMs (bank A)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors. Each SM has 128 FP32/INT32 CUDA cores, 4 fifth-generation Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file and 128 KB unified L1/shared memory. The grid is symbolic — this model does not claim an exact layout. Click **Open SM** to look inside.

specs.label: SM count
specs.value: symbolic grid; 188 enabled, see die specs

components.name: GDDR7 chips (left bank)
components.desc: Discrete GDDR7 packages, surface-mounted (clamshell: front + back of the PCB) — no interposer, no TSV stack. 96 GB total with ECC, 3x the RTX 5090's 32GB (same die, but the 5090 has no ECC and a single-sided, non-clamshell layout) and 2x the previous-gen L40S's 48GB GDDR6.

specs.label: Chip arrangement
specs.value: Drawn as 16 packages per side (left+right); real card uses clamshell mounting (front+back) for 96 GB — exact per-chip density not disclosed

components.name: GDDR7 chips (right bank)
components.desc: Second bank of GDDR7 packages, mirroring the left bank.

components.name: L1 Data Cache / Shared Memory
components.desc: 128 KB unified, programmable L1 data cache / shared memory per SM. Operand tiles for the Tensor Core and ray/triangle data for the RT Core both stage here. Unlike data-center Blackwell (B200), RTX Blackwell's SM has no separate Tensor Memory (TMEM) — accumulation happens straight in the register file.

components.name: Tensor Core (5th gen)
components.desc: 4 fifth-generation Tensor Cores per SM. New FP4 support doubles throughput over FP8 and halves memory footprint for quantized inference — the same Tensor Core generation as B200, minus the TMEM-based tile sizes B200's datacenter SM supports.

specs.label: FP4 Tensor (per GPU)
specs.value: 2,015.2 TFLOPS dense / 4,030.4 TFLOPS sparse, FP32 accumulate

specs.label: FP8 Tensor (per GPU)
specs.value: 1,007.6 TFLOPS dense / 2,015.2 TFLOPS sparse, FP32 accumulate

components.name: Register file
components.desc: Per-thread registers, one 64 KB slice (16,384 x 32-bit) per SM sub-partition, 256 KB total per SM. With no TMEM, Tensor Core accumulators land here directly.

specs.label: Size (per SM)
specs.value: 256 KB (4 x 64 KB, 16,384 x 32-bit per partition)

components.name: Warp scheduler + CUDA cores
components.desc: Each of the SM's 4 partitions has its own L0 instruction cache, warp scheduler and dispatch unit issuing 32 threads/clk. Scalar FP32/INT32 CUDA cores run the epilogue: bias, activation, requantize.

specs.label: Partitions per SM
specs.value: 4, each with its own warp scheduler

steps.text: 1. Weights and KV cache sit in 96 GB of GDDR7 ECC memory across a 512-bit bus — 3x the RTX 5090's 32GB (same die, no ECC) and 2x the previous-gen L40S's 48GB GDDR6.
2. One of the 512-bit GDDR7 memory controllers reads the request, reaching up to 1,792 GB/s aggregate across the whole GPU.
3. Data lands in the single 128 MB L2 cache shared by every SM on this monolithic die — no die-to-die coherency link needed, unlike B200's two-die MCM.
4. The request reaches one of 188 enabled SMs (4 disabled from the full 192-SM GB202 die for yield).
5. Operand tiles stage in the 128 KB unified L1 Data Cache / Shared Memory — RTX Blackwell has no separate Tensor Memory (TMEM); that's a data-center Blackwell (B200) feature only.
6. The 5th-generation Tensor Core multiplies the tiles. New FP4 support doubles throughput over FP8 and halves the memory footprint for quantized inference.
7. Partial sums accumulate directly in the register file (FP32 accumulate) — no dedicated accumulator memory like B200's TMEM.
8. Epilogue: the warp scheduler issues CUDA cores to apply bias, activation and requantize back to FP4/FP8.
9. Results write back through L2 to GDDR7. With no NVLink on this card, multi-GPU scaling goes over PCIe 5.0 x16 only — well below B200's 1.8 TB/s NVLink 5 per GPU.
10. For visualization workloads, the 4th-gen RT Core traces rays with Mega Geometry support for massive scenes — fixed-function hardware absent on AI-only parts like B200.
11. ROPs and texture units finish the rasterized frame — professional visualization stays a first-class workload on this card, unlike data-center-only GPUs.
12. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can split the card into up to 4 isolated instances (e.g. 4 x 24 GB) for secure multi-tenant inference serving.
